messages:
Riley Gomez: Quick recap from the on-call bridge — thanks to everyone who jumped in. We mitigated the surge by throttling new model handshakes and reverting the canary. Root cause looks like a shard-namespace mismatch in the sticky assignment logic that surfaced only when multiple reconnects and a model restart coincided during rollout. More notes below.

incident-bot: [ALERT] 2024-12-05T01:17:08Z -> Elevated error rate and queued requests on /v1/chat-stream (svc=runtime-prod-eu). Paging on-call.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout 0xfeedface started 2024-12-05T01:02Z, pause detected 2024-12-05T01:20Z, rollback completed 2024-12-05T01:32Z.

Owen Li: Observations from bridge: canary changes adjusted the shard prefixing for backend caches to prefer locality. Under a burst of reconnects (we saw ~800 concurrent reconnects over 3m) a race allowed two nodes to claim the same logical prefix, causing frequent orphan evictions and backpressure on the model pool. Backpressure -> queuing -> gateway timeouts -> 502/504. I attached a short grep of the logs showing duplicate-namespace allocations.

Owen Li: Local repro (summary):
```
# simulate concurrent reconnects and restarts
parallel_clients = 500
for i in range(parallel_clients):
  client.connect(id=f'u{i}', model='rwd-l2')
  if i % 50 == 0:
    restart_model_worker()
  client.disconnect()
# observe namespace-claim warnings in logs
```
Logs: `shard_assigner: namespace_conflict shard=15 prefix=ns-7` repeated.

Marco Torres: Customer impact: small subset of hosted customers hit visible latency spikes, two accounts observed automatic failover to fallback models which caused degraded quality. No billing anomalies. I'll prepare a short CSV table of impacted API keys to attach.

Sana Patel: Can we confirm timeline for a customer note? CS wants a short status update ASAP, then a fuller RCA within 48h. Also legal asked if any Private/Dedicated pools were included in the canary cohort.

Riley Gomez: Quick answer: only hosted eu-west-1 canary pool was affected; Dedicated and Private pools were not on the canary tag. Marco, please verify with infra and list any accounts that had Dedicated capacity — we should exclude them from the outreach.

Owen Li: Proposed short-term fixes we applied: 1) paused rollout; 2) rate-limited handshake traffic to 50 req/s per node; 3) forced deterministic namespace mapping in the assignment layer to avoid collisions while we build a full fix. Permanent fix plan: remove non-deterministic leader election path for prefix claims, add a consensus step, and add a unit/integration test for reconnect storms.

Riley Gomez: Postmortem meeting proposal: Fri 10:00 CET (45m). Agenda: incident timeline, detailed RCA, test coverage gaps, remediation plan, customer comm sign-off. Can everyone make it?

Sana Patel: I can do Fri 10:00 CET. I'll draft the customer-facing status page blurb and a template email for impacted customers. Suggest we include apology, high-level cause, what we changed immediately, and what we'll do to prevent recurrence.

Marco Torres: Suggested action items (initial):
- P1: Implement deterministic prefix allocation + unit tests -> owner: Owen -> due: 2024-12-12
- P2: Add reconnect-storm scenario to pre-rollout CI (chaos test) -> owner: Eng-SRE (assigned: Riley) -> due: 2024-12-19
- P3: Emergency throttle capability documented in runbook -> owner: Riley -> due: 2024-12-09
- P4: Customer impact CSV + account outreach list -> owner: Marco -> due: 2024-12-06
- P5: Draft customer-facing RCA and obtain legal/security review -> owner: Sana -> due: 2024-12-07
Please shout if dates look tight.

Riley Gomez: I'll take P3 and coordinate with on-call owners to add the throttle toggle to the emergency runbook. Owen, please link the PR when you open it so I can cite the fix in the postmortem. Marco, if you can get the CSV before EOD tomorrow that helps CS prioritize outreach.

incident-bot: [BRIDGE_NOTE] Bridge closed 2024-12-05T02:02:30Z. Duration: 45m.

Sana Patel: Draft status page snippet (short):
"2024-12-05 01:02 UTC — We experienced increased errors and latency for a subset of text/chat customers due to a shard namespace collision introduced during a canary rollout. We paused and rolled back the canary and applied emergency mitigation; normal service resumed by 02:02 UTC. A detailed RCA will be shared with impacted customers within 48 hours."

Sana Patel: Draft customer email (template):
Hi <CustomerName>,

We wanted to follow up on the service degradation you may have seen on 2024-12-05. Our engineers traced the issue to a shard namespace collision that occurred during a canary deployment, which led to increased errors and fallback behavior for some requests. We rolled back the canary and applied mitigations; service returned to normal by 02:02 UTC. We are preparing a technical report and will share it by 2024-12-07. If you'd like a walkthrough of the impact on your account, please let me know and we can schedule a 1:1.

Marco Torres: Security/legal check: I ran a quick scan and there is no evidence of data exfiltration or secret exposure. Logs show internal shard assignment warnings only. I'll include a short security statement in the postmortem.

Owen Li: Follow-ups: I'll open the deterministic prefix PR by EOD Mon and add the reconnect storm regression test to the CI. Will ping here when CI green. Also adding metric: `namespace_conflict_count` and an alert threshold > 1/min -> owner: Riley -> ETA 2024-12-09.

Riley Gomez: Confirmed — postmortem Fri 10:00 CET. Sana to circulate customer drafts by Fri 14:00 CET for review. Owners to update status in the incidents doc and mark items done when complete. Ping here for any blockers. :white_check_mark:
